amendment: After the v0.1 request, diagnostic output exposed a one-base indexing error. Official model source confirms that positive-strand donor tracks label the last exonic base, while junctions start at the first intronic base. The original v0.1 config is archived unchanged. This correction changes interpretation only; the API request parameters are identical and no repeat request was made.
purpose: Exploratory follow-up to the completed four-variant pilot: test the signed effect of A>C at the annotated UBASH3A donor, and inspect CD4 splice usage and junctions

primary_endpoint.comparison: ALT probability minus REF probability at the last exonic nucleotide; report the corrected result as exploratory, alongside the original v0.1 reading

annotation.interpretation: Variant is at intron +3. The shared boundary is exon 9 in ENST00000291535.12 and exon 10 in ENST00000319294.11. Ensembl release 116 is an independent boundary annotation, not a claim of matching every GENCODE v46 model transcript.

secondary_endpoints: Signed SPLICE_SITE_USAGE change at the primary donor for each returned positive-strand CD4 track, with assay names retained

All returned positive-strand junctions touching either the annotated donor boundary or the downstream exon boundary, plus any junction crossing both boundaries; outer join REF and ALT, leaving absent predictions missing rather than zero
limitations: Selected after observing the first pilot and published splicing evidence; not an independent validation or a discovery
No negative-control set, statistical test, stimulation-matched assay, or held-out model in this follow-up
Splice-site probability is a model classification output, not a measured fraction of retained intron
Usage and junction signals are distinct endpoints; neither alone establishes a transcript isoform, protein effect, or clinical benefit
